source_title: COTRAV BLACK enters India’s luxury live-entertainment market, to debut at A R Rahman concert - ET TravelWorld
source_excerpt: COTRAV BLACK, an invite-only luxury live-experiences platform, is entering India’s entertainment market with a proposition centred on exclusive access, curated hospitality and private VIP settings for affluent audiences attending major concerts and other live events.The platform will make its debut at A R Rahman’s concert at Mumbai’s Jio World Garden on November 1, 2026. It plans to host invitation-only VIP enclosures at select concerts, sporting events and cultural gatherings, targeting business leaders, entrepreneurs, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs) and ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs).Backed by the business group behind travel management company COTRAV, the new venture draws on the group’s experience in managing travel and logistics for large events, weddings and concerts. COTRAV BLACK will operate as a distinct brand focused on premium live-entertainment experiences.The launch comes amid rapid growth in India’s organised live-events industry. The FICCI-EY Media & Entertainment Report 2026 estimates that the segment grew 44% in 2025 to ₹14,500 crore and is projected to reach ₹19,600 crore by 2028. The report attributes the expansion to increased spending on ticketed concerts, weddings, government events and religious gatherings.Against this backdrop, COTRAV BLACK is positioning itself around a specific audience requirement: attending large-scale entertainment events while retaining greater privacy, comfort and control over the overall experience.Vinod Kumar Sah, Co-founder and CTO of COTRAV, said the growth in the scale of live entertainment had created a need for more tailored experiences for senior executives and high-profile audiences.“COTRAV BLACK is our answer to that gap. We are creating an exclusive social setting where the country's most influential people can enjoy exceptional live performances, surrounded by the right company and the finest hospitality,” Sah said.The planned enclosures will feature curated guest lists, personalised hospitality and food and beverage offerings. The company aims to provide a more intimate setting within the larger event environment, addressing concerns around crowd management, access and privacy that it believes can deter some affluent audiences from attending major concerts.Beyond individual attendees, the platform is also looking to develop a commercial proposition for brands, financial institutions and large enterprises seeking access to high-value customers and business partners.COTRAV BLACK plans to explore selective brand partnerships that would place participating organisations within these curated social settings. Such collaborations are expected to form part of its longer-term commercial strategy, with the company seeking to build associations around premium cultural and entertainment occasions.The business model would bring together event access, hospitality and corporate relationship-building, creating an additional proposition for organisations looking to engage affluent consumers outside conventional marketing and networking environments.However, the company has not disclosed the scale of its planned event calendar, pricing structure, investment in the platform or details of confirmed commercial partners.With its first activation scheduled for November 1, COTRAV BLACK’s initial offering will provide an early indication of how the platform translates its invite-only positioning into an operating model for India’s expanding live-entertainment market.
